batch_size_mismatched_T4_vs_dav2_B1.description: VDA-S at T=4 vs DA-V2 at B=1 -- DIFFERENT batch composition on GPU
batch_size_mismatched_T4_vs_dav2_B1.verdict: Small nonzero difference -- confirmed (via the T1-vs-T1-repeat determinism check, 0.0 diff, and the T1-exact-match result above) to be ordinary GPU batch-size-dependent floating-point non-associativity (different cudnn/attention kernel selection for batch=4 vs batch=1), not a defect in the init logic. An earlier run with cudnn.benchmark left at its default (nondeterministic) setting showed a larger 0.0095 max-abs-diff at T=4 for the same reason -- resolved by setting cudnn.deterministic=True, and by the T1 test isolating the init logic from batch-size effects entirely.

T4_repeat_determinism.description: Fable's tidiness request, 2026-08-27: the same T=4-batch forward run twice in a row, same process, same inputs -- completes the isolation alongside the T1-repeat check already covering the T=1 case.
T4_repeat_determinism.verdict: EXACT match -- T=4 forward passes are themselves fully deterministic (cudnn.deterministic=True); the T4-vs-T1 discrepancy above is purely a batch-size effect, not run-to-run noise at either batch size.

overall_verdict: PASS -- the required reproduction check holds exactly when batch size is matched (the correct comparison for validating init correctness); the residual T>1 discrepancy is characterized and attributed to benign GPU batch-size floating-point effects, not a bug in models/vda_net.py.
caveat: VAL-01 training itself will run at batch/clip sizes >1 and will therefore inherit this same benign batch-size-dependent floating-point variance -- irrelevant to the 5%-AbsRel reproduction target, which operates at a much coarser scale, but noted here so a future reader does not mistake normal GPU numerics for a regression.
